question: Can monotonic regularized defender boosting remove backwards evidence effects without sacrificing out-of-time accuracy?
scope: Defender head only; unchanged rows, features, targets, priors, scaling and isotonic calibration protocol. No source or market additions.
control: Existing locked GBM with saved trained artifacts; verify training-frame cache keys and current Tarkowski 0.695 reproduction before comparing.

expected.monotonicity: zero violations on the five constrained features
expected.personal_update_tarkowski: fall of 0 to 0.02 when applying the Chelsea evidence update with experience/spread/context fixed
expected.weekly_evidence_p95: at least 20% smaller absolute changes on 2025 (diagnostic, not an accuracy substitute)

ship_rule.log_loss: improve at least 0.001 on A or B, and neither split worsens by more than 0.002
ship_rule.brier: neither split worsens by more than 0.002
ship_rule.auc: neither split drops by more than 0.01
ship_rule.mechanism: zero single-feature increasing-evidence reversals in validation audits; Tarkowski joint evidence update cannot increase probability when all five evidence features fall
ship_rule.failure: retain incumbent default, retain experiment evidence, report rejection; do not select more parameters on these held-out results

calibration: Same incumbent 5-fold shuffled stratified OOF isotonic fit. This preserves the control comparison; temporal calibration is a separate potential experiment.
weekly_diagnostic: For adjacent appearances in held-out season, score the two pre-match evidence vectors using the same split model and the earlier row's nuisance/context features. This isolates changing evidence; it does not measure weekly model-refit instability.
limitations: Historical detailed positions and transfer estimators inherit existing pipeline assumptions
No claim that constraints force all real-world weekly ratings to decline after every unsuccessful match
